one_line: An in-browser runtime that diagnoses and reversibly repairs web performance problems through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Observes live browser performance telemetry, applies bounded DOM/CSS remediation, and records provenance for each mutation.
leverage_rationale: The claimed in-process access to live PerformanceObserver data and direct reversible remediation is substantially more reliable than an external agent clicking a UI, though the packet does not demonstrate the full flow in video.
leverage_evidence: About text describes seven typed WebMCP tools registered in the page.
Claimed no-reload repair preserves live form state and acts on the page being observed.
execution_rationale: The concept and implementation claims are coherent, but evidence is packaging plus frame sheets without transcript or recorded end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported.
About text gives a concrete before/after latency claim and SLSA-shaped receipts.
impact_rationale: Web developers and users of heavy web interfaces have a concrete performance problem, and automated evidence-gated repair could provide meaningful value.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies dropped frames and high input latency as the target problem.
Claims a reduction from roughly 470 ms blocking to roughly 1 ms handler return.
creativity_rationale: A self-healing runtime combining browser-native telemetry, reversible remediation, and tamper-evident provenance is an ambitious and memorable WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Self-healing directly inside the observed page is a distinctive interaction model.
Per-mutation provenance and authority tracking add unusual depth.
usability_note: Potentially low-friction because it runs in the active page, but operational safety and repair review are not visually established.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; several important claims are unverified in the packet.
standouts: Evidence-gated, reversible performance repair with provenance.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and originality; Stage 2 should verify the claimed repair and audit trail.

one_line: A shared whiteboard where an agent reads and edits the live canvas using state-dependent tools.
what_it_does: Lets people and agents create notes, shapes, diagrams, and connections on one Excalidraw-based board with shared undo history.
leverage_rationale: Structured graph state and tools that appear or disappear with board state materially outperform pixel interpretation and avoid invalid operations on an empty board.
leverage_evidence: About text says the agent receives graph state rather than screenshots.
Tool availability changes based on whether the board has elements or enough shapes to connect.
execution_rationale: The described contracts, shared canvas functions, and teardown approach form a coherent product, with live demo reported but no video transcript.
execution_evidence: Five named tools are described with conditional availability.
Agent edits and hand-drawn shapes share one board and undo history.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals making diagrams have a clear need for turning notes into structured visuals, and shared agent participation is useful.
impact_evidence: Concrete workflow starts from sticky notes and produces a labeled diagram.
No install, configuration, or API key is claimed.
creativity_rationale: Treating the agent as a participant in a stateful whiteboard, with a dynamically changing tool surface, is a fresh interaction model.
creativity_evidence: State-dependent tool registration is central rather than cosmetic.
The agent uses the same canvas functions and shared undo model as humans.
usability_note: No-install shared editing is compelling; usability of diagram generation is not independently demonstrated by video.
red_flags: No video submitted; visual evidence is limited to frame sheets.
standouts: Conditional tool surface tied to live board state.
advance_reason: Clear WebMCP delta and strong interaction concept; verify live agent edits and tool changes.

one_line: A constrained 96-well plate layout tool that lets scientists encode local knowledge and have an agent safely reflow experiments.
what_it_does: Locks controls, blocks unavailable wells, reflows unlocked experiments, validates constraints, and emits an operation receipt.
leverage_rationale: A bounded semantic reflow operation over shared structured plate state is materially safer and more precise than coordinate clicking or pixel inference.
leverage_evidence: Transcript reports three narrow site tools and one atomic reflow operation.
24 placements moved while locked controls and blocked wells were preserved.
execution_rationale: The packet supplies unusually complete end-to-end evidence: human constraints, violations, agent invocation, result counts, preservation checks, receipt, and test claims.
execution_evidence: Transcript explicitly reports two violations becoming zero.
Transcript reports 136 automated tests and five of five fresh site-tool trials.
impact_rationale: Scientists using 96-well plates have a concrete safety-sensitive layout problem; the product preserves domain judgment while removing tedious repair work.
impact_evidence: Controls B2/B3 and unavailable wells B6/B7 are concrete constraints.
Demonstrated result moves 24 experiments without violating constraints.
creativity_rationale: The local-judgment/global-repair framing is an original, well-scoped application of agents to scientific layout constraints.
creativity_evidence: Human encodes facts software cannot infer; agent performs global repair.
Receipt makes the operation checkable.
usability_note: Natural-language request plus visible validation and receipt supports safe reviewable use.
standouts: Strong end-to-end evidence and safety-preserving semantic operation.
advance_reason: Best-evidenced packet with high leverage, impact, and execution.

one_line: A source-backed municipal planning research desk shared by people and browser agents.
what_it_does: Searches, lists changes, inspects filing-level records, and stages an evidence-backed brief for human review.
leverage_rationale: Structured filing-level search and staging reduce ambiguity across scattered municipal records; a general agent could perform the work but less reliably and with weaker shared state.
leverage_evidence: About text describes four completed WebMCP calls: search, list changes, inspect, and stage.
Each result preserves official sources and distinct filing statuses.
execution_rationale: The described workflow is coherent and careful, but there is no video or transcript and visual claims are not independently checkable.
execution_evidence: A three-filing brief is claimed staged for human review.
Packet reports five gallery images and a live demo.
impact_rationale: Land and development teams, lenders, title professionals, journalists, and planners face a real problem in tracking procedural changes across fragmented records.
impact_evidence: Concrete Bentonville/Rogers examples distinguish withdrawn and recommended filings.
Human review is required and nothing is published or sent.
creativity_rationale: The evidence handoff between researcher and agent, focused on quiet procedural changes rather than generic search, is a fresh and purposeful angle.
creativity_evidence: Filing-level provenance and dated change detection are central.
The product explicitly avoids agenda-wording-only heuristics.
usability_note: Review-first staging and source visibility support professional trust.
red_flags: No submitted video; end-to-end operation is claimed rather than shown in transcript.
standouts: Strong provenance and human-review boundary for civic records.
advance_reason: Credible high-impact niche workflow with meaningful agent-state benefits.

one_line: A versioned evidence workspace where humans and agents build and verify the same accountable case.
what_it_does: Manages claim revisions, evidence, provenance, conflicts, deterministic evaluations, and export through structured tools.
leverage_rationale: Shared versioned state, provenance, uncertainty, and decision lineage are difficult to maintain through general UI automation; the structured tools are central to the product.
leverage_evidence: Six tools cover reading a case, revising claims, adding evidence, conflicts, evaluation, and export.
About text explicitly contrasts shared application state with an agent's hidden parallel case.
execution_rationale: The architecture and governance model are coherent, but the packet has no video and demo status is unknown, so completion is insufficiently evidenced.
execution_evidence: Detailed Distillation Protocol and case data model are described.
Public repository is reported, but runtime demonstration is not.
impact_rationale: Researchers, journalists, and decision-makers have a real need for evidence-backed, challengeable web intelligence rather than opaque conclusions.
impact_evidence: Explicit support for provenance, uncertainty, conflicts, and deterministic verdicts.
Human and agent are described as building one inspectable case.
creativity_rationale: The governance boundary and bidirectional distillation protocol are an ambitious original interaction model for browsing agents.
creativity_evidence: Versioned claim/evidence lineage is treated as a first-class product object.
Outbound actions are scoped and inspectable rather than silently executed.
usability_note: Accountability features may improve trust, but no usable flow is demonstrated.
red_flags: Demo status unknown and no video submitted; substantial claims are unverified.
advance_reason: High conceptual value; advance for runtime verification because execution evidence is thin.

one_line: A real-time collaborative canvas that makes an agent a normal room participant using the same edit API as humans.
what_it_does: Supports shared canvas rooms, named agents with cursors, typed edits, shared undo, and HTML export.
leverage_rationale: Using the exact multiplayer action path and shared state gives the agent semantic canvas operations and real-time collaboration that UI driving cannot match as reliably.
leverage_evidence: Every tool reportedly calls the same Socket.IO events as human edits.
Server has no privileged human/agent path; undo/redo is shared.
execution_rationale: The product architecture and scope are concrete, but there is no video and the live demo claim is not backed by transcript evidence.
execution_evidence: Claimed Vite/React/TypeScript client, Node/Express/Socket.IO server, Postgres state and event log.
About text reports a from-scratch realtime canvas and export_html.
impact_rationale: Distributed teams and creators can benefit from an agent collaborating directly in a visual workspace rather than returning detached edits.
impact_evidence: Realtime rooms, live cursors, shared undo, and export are described as working product capabilities.
creativity_rationale: Making the agent a believable peer with identity and cursor in a multiplayer canvas is a memorable, deeply integrated interaction model.
creativity_evidence: One code path for human and agent edits.
Agent identity, color, and cursor are part of the room model.
usability_note: Shared undo and familiar canvas affordances are promising; no direct workflow video was submitted.
red_flags: Base canvas reportedly predated WebMCP; packet does not establish exact new-work scope beyond the integration.
standouts: Agent as a first-class multiplayer peer, not a privileged automation path.
advance_reason: Excellent leverage and interaction design; verify live collaboration and scope eligibility.

one_line: A policy control plane that wraps WebMCP tools to protect data and require human approval for risky actions.
what_it_does: Applies data transformation/tokenization, confirmation gates, and agent posture policies through an SDK and management console.
leverage_rationale: Policy enforcement at the WebMCP tool boundary can provide consistent structured controls that generic UI automation may bypass, though the concept remains an infrastructure layer around existing tools.
leverage_evidence: SDK wraps imperative WebMCP functions and injects controls.
Policies include deterministic tokenization and on-page confirmation before destructive actions.
execution_rationale: The policy model is detailed, but demo status is unknown and there is no video or transcript demonstrating enforcement.
execution_evidence: Four gallery images and a public repository are reported.
Management console and multiple policy types are described.
impact_rationale: Organizations exposing sensitive internal applications have a concrete need to control agent access without destroying useful reasoning context.
impact_evidence: Examples cover names, SSNs, credit cards, health-record dates, and irreversible deletion.
Consistent replacement tokens preserve cross-record reasoning while hiding sensitive values.
creativity_rationale: Privacy-preserving structured transformations plus agent posture and human confirmation form a thoughtful security treatment of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Tokenization preserves referential reasoning rather than simply blocking data.
Multiple policy layers address data, action, and agent identity.
usability_note: Central policy management could simplify governance, but enforcement UX is not demonstrated.
red_flags: Demo status unknown; no video evidence of policies being enforced.
standouts: Privacy transformations designed to preserve agent utility.
advance_reason: High practical impact; advance to verify the wrapper and actual policy enforcement.

one_line: A job-search workspace where an agent discovers, compares, saves, and drafts opportunities while the human keeps final control.
what_it_does: Searches listings, reads job details and candidate profile, saves matches, retrieves saved jobs, and drafts tailored applications.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, profile retrieval, and save/draft operations reduce repetitive job-search work, though a general agent could achieve much of the same with moderate UI friction.
leverage_evidence: Named agent capabilities cover search, details, profile, saving, saved jobs, and drafting.
Applying is explicitly kept as a human decision.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the live demo plus five gallery images suggest a substantial implementation, but no video transcript demonstrates completion.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
CV upload and parsing, editable profile, live listings, and saved opportunities are described.
impact_rationale: Job seekers face a real repetitive discovery and comparison burden, and the human-in-the-loop boundary fits consequential applications.
impact_evidence: Concrete workflow compares listings against the user's skills and saves strongest matches.
Human remains responsible for judgment and final application decisions.
creativity_rationale: A well-executed human-agent job workspace is useful but largely a familiar application of agent assistance to a known category.
creativity_evidence: First-class agent framing and explicit no-auto-apply boundary.
CV parsing and tailored draft support add a practical angle.
usability_note: Familiar workspace with reviewable saved jobs and drafts should be approachable.
red_flags: No video submitted; tool invocation and end-to-end draft flow are not directly evidenced.
standouts: Appropriate human control over consequential application submission.
advance_reason: Clear audience and useful workflow; leverage and originality are moderate rather than exceptional.

one_line: An agent-driven generator for stylized multilingual app-store screenshots.
what_it_does: Launches an app in a simulator, captures screenshots, and stylizes them for store listings in multiple languages.
leverage_rationale: Automation across simulator launch, capture, localization, and styling can remove repetitive work, but the packet does not establish a WebMCP-specific advantage over other automation APIs.
leverage_evidence: About text claims autonomous agent launch, screenshot, and stylization workflow.
WebMCP is described mainly as avoiding API token setup.
execution_rationale: The submission explicitly says the application could not be tested, and no video or frame sheets were submitted; execution is therefore thinly evidenced.
execution_evidence: About text states the creator ran out of credits and could not test the application.
No submitted video and zero gallery images are reported.
impact_rationale: App developers have a real tedious localization and store-asset production task, but delivered value is uncertain because the product was not tested.
impact_evidence: Clear target use case: multilingual app-store and Play Store screenshot generation.
Creator identifies screenshot production as tedious.
creativity_rationale: Autonomous store screenshot generation is a reasonable new angle, but the concept is not deeply evidenced or especially novel relative to automation tools.
creativity_evidence: Combines simulator capture with stylization and multilingual output.
Future plans indicate core options and project tools remain to be added.
usability_note: Untested state and missing output evidence make usability unclear and likely poor at submission time.
red_flags: Creator says it could not be tested.
No video, frame sheets, or gallery images.
advance_reason: Execution and WebMCP leverage are too weakly evidenced, with an explicit inability to test.

one_line: MODE lets users reshape a website's presentation and accessibility by describing preferences to an agent.
what_it_does: Applies persistent display preferences such as typography, contrast, clutter reduction, image visibility, and sorting to a storefront.
leverage_rationale: A semantic preference layer lets an agent alter presentation while preserving site-owned facts and functionality; general UI automation could attempt this but would be fragile and difficult to persist.
leverage_evidence: About text describes capabilities intentionally exposed by the website for agent adaptation.
Preferences are stored in cookies and target multiple coordinated presentation changes.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent and supported by ten gallery images and a live demo, but no video or transcript verifies the full flow.
execution_evidence: Live demo, public repository, and ten gallery images are reported.
Concrete Cartly storefront scenario and preference examples are described.
impact_rationale: People with low vision, ADHD, price-sensitive shopping goals, or strong presentation preferences have real needs that current site controls only partly address.
impact_evidence: Examples include larger text, stronger contrast, fewer distractions, hiding images, and category/price sorting.
Guiding principle preserves trusted content while giving users control over experience.
creativity_rationale: The inversion of site-owned functionality and user-owned presentation is a compelling, memorable interaction model for agent-native accessibility and personalization.
creativity_evidence: MODE treats conversational reshaping as a reusable preference layer.
The fictional dense storefront is used to demonstrate coordinated transformations.
usability_note: Natural-language personalization and persistence could be accessible to nontechnical users; live behavior is not video-proven.
red_flags: No submitted video; agent invocation details and persistence need live verification.
standouts: Strong user-agency framing for accessibility and personalization.
advance_reason: Meaningful audience value and creative concept with enough packaging evidence to merit verification.
